Coverage, definitions & methodology Read before comparing

This dataset covers the original top 15 energy-consuming countries plus Croatia. Rankings on this site describe this selected sample, not every country. Missing prices are unavailable, not zero.

Prices are electricity retail rates, not total energy costs or dedicated industrial tariffs. Business rates assume 1,000,000 kWh of annual use. Prices include supply, transmission, distribution, taxes and fees. USD values are those recorded by the source; exchange-rate dates are unspecified and currency changes can affect comparisons.

Prices: December 2025. Consumption and energy mix: 2024. Total-energy production and trade: 2023. Electricity production and trade: 2024. Sources were accessed in September 2026. Each metric retains its own year.

Electricity mix describes domestic generation, not electricity consumed. “Other” combines nuclear and other renewables and must not be read as all renewable. Oil & other fossil is a combined electricity category. Primary-energy shares use the substitution method, exclude traditional biomass, and cannot be multiplied by the IEA domestic-production totals.

Electricity generation and trade use EIA data, while generation mix uses OWID/Ember; totals can differ. Gross trade measures cross-border flows. Net imports equal imports minus exports. Positive means net importing; negative means net exporting. Energy mix and trade comparisons do not establish causes of electricity prices.
